40815-prices-of-books-an-inquiry-into-th.title: England At Different Periods
40815-prices-of-books-an-inquiry-into-th.creator: Henry B. Wheatley, F.S.A.
40815-prices-of-books-an-inquiry-into-th.description: A book by Henry B. Wheatley, F.S.A.. afforded for books which at an earlier period would have been out of the question; and not less so that while some classes of books had risen in worth with the enhanced standard of wealth, others had accommodated themselves to the requirements of the poor. We should trace the effect of mechanical improvements in diminishing the prices of things, and of fashion and curiosity in augmenting them.

49481-twice-killed-a-farce-in-one-act.title: One Act
49481-twice-killed-a-farce-in-one-act.creator: John Oxenford
49481-twice-killed-a-farce-in-one-act.description: A book by John Oxenford. Yes, and Reginald de Mowbray is a much prettier name than Ralph Reckless, but where was I? Well, the young lady's governess finds out the correspondence, and very properly sends her to her guardians, who takes her into the country, also very properly; give up this scheme, sir--

56781-midnight-sunbeams-or-bits-of-trave.title: Of The Norseman
56781-midnight-sunbeams-or-bits-of-trave.creator: _Edwin Coolidge Kimball_
56781-midnight-sunbeams-or-bits-of-trave.description: A book by _Edwin Coolidge Kimball_. It was on a charming day in June, after an hour’s railway ride from Hamburg, that we arrived at Lübeck—the starting point of our journey through Scandinavia. Lübeck is the smallest of the three independent Hanseatic towns of the German Empire, both Hamburg and Bremen far surpassing her in size and importance, yet at one time she stood at the head of the Hanseatic League—the alliance of the great commercial towns of North Germany.

arxiv-2102-01935.title: Sensitivity Analysis for Unmeasured Confounding via Effect Extrapolation
arxiv-2102-01935.creator: Wen Wei Loh, Stijn Vansteelandt
arxiv-2102-01935.description: Abstract Inferring the causal effect of a non-randomly assigned exposure on an outcome requires adjusting for common causes of the exposure and outcome to avoid biased conclusions. Notwithstanding the efforts investigators routinely make to measure and adjust for such common causes (or confounders), some confounders typically remain unmeasured, raising the prospect of biased inference in observational studies.

arxiv-2112-11124.title: Learning Human Motion Prediction via Stochastic Differential Equations DOI: 10.1145/1122445.1122456 Conference: Proceedings of the 29th ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 20–24, 2021; Virtual Event, China. Chengdu ’21: Learning Human Motion Prediction via Stochastic Differential Equ
arxiv-2112-11124.creator: Kedi Lyu, Zhenguang Liu, Shuang Wu, Haipeng Chen, Xuhong Zhang, Yuyu Yin
arxiv-2112-11124.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Kedi Lyu, Zhenguang Liu, Shuang Wu, Haipeng Chen, Xuhong Zhang, Yuyu Yin. Human motion understanding and prediction is an integral aspect in our pursuit of machine intelligence and human-machine interaction systems. Current methods typically pursue a kinematics modeling approach, relying heavily upon prior anatomical knowledge and constraints. However, such an approach is hard to generalize to different skeletal model representations, and also tends to be inadequate in accounting for the dynamic range and complexity of motion, thus hindering predictive accuracy.

arxiv-2207-13372.title: Charged Higgs induced 5 and 6 lepton signatures from heavy neutrinos at the LHC Preprint: EPHOU-22-015, OU-HET 1151, APCTP Pre2022-019
arxiv-2207-13372.creator: Arindam Das, Shinya Kanemura, Prasenjit Sanyal
arxiv-2207-13372.description: Abstract We propose an anomaly free gauged U ( 1 ) (1) extension of the SM where three right handed heavy neutrinos, being charged under the general U ( 1 ) (1) gauge group, are introduced to explain the origin of the tiny neutrino mass through the seesaw mechanism after the general U ( 1 ) (1) symmetry is broken.

arxiv-2211-08009.title: Nonequilibrium Phase Transition To Temporal Oscillations In Mean-Field Spin Models
arxiv-2211-08009.creator: Laura Guislain, Eric Bertin
arxiv-2211-08009.description: Abstract We propose a mean-field theory to describe the nonequilibrium phase transition to a spontaneously oscillating state in spin models. A nonequilibrium generalization of the Landau free energy is obtained from the joint distribution of the magnetization and its smoothed stochastic time derivative. The order parameter of the transition is a Hamiltonian, whose nonzero value signals the onset of oscillations.

arxiv-2310-05675.title: Prediction of Gaussian Volterra Processes with Compound Poisson Jumps
arxiv-2310-05675.creator: Hamidreza Maleki Almani, Foad Shokrollahi, Tommi Sottinen
arxiv-2310-05675.description: Abstract . We consider a Gaussian Volterra process with compound Poisson jumps and derive its prediction law. 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 91G20; 91G80; 60G22 1. Introduction We are interested in a mixed process X=G+J , where the continuous part G is a so-called Gaussian Volterra process. In older terminology these are processes that admit canonical representation of multiplicity one.

arxiv-2402-11935.title: Computing epsilon multiplicities in graded algebras
arxiv-2402-11935.creator: Suprajo Das, Saipriya Dubey, Sudeshna Roy, Jugal K. Verma
arxiv-2402-11935.description: Abstract . This article investigates the computational aspects of the ε \varepsilon -multiplicity. Primarily, we show that the ε \varepsilon -multiplicity of a homogeneous ideal I I in a two-dimensional standard graded domain of finite type over an algebraically closed field of arbitrary characteristic, is always a rational number.

arxiv-2503-24140.title: Reinforcement Learning for Safe Autonomous Two Device Navigation of Cerebral Vessels in Mechanical Thrombectomy Thanks: Citation : Robertshaw, H., Jackson, B., Wang., J., et al. Reinforcement learning for safe autonomous two device navigation of cerebral vessels in mechanical thrombectomy. Int J CAR
arxiv-2503-24140.creator: Harry Robertshaw, Benjamin Jackson, Jiaheng Wang, Hadi Sadati, Alejandro Granados, Thomas C Booth, Lennart Karstensen
arxiv-2503-24140.description: Abstract Purpose: Autonomous systems in mechanical thrombectomy (MT) hold promise for reducing procedure times, minimizing radiation exposure, and enhancing patient safety. However, current reinforcement learning (RL) methods only reach the carotid arteries, are not generalizable to other patient vasculatures, and do not consider safety.

arxiv-2504-01106.title: Quantum Resetting Protocols Based on Synchronizing Words
arxiv-2504-01106.creator: Jȩdrzej Stempin, Jan Wójcik, Andrzej Grudka, Marcin Karczewski, Paweł Kurzyński, Antoni Wójcik
arxiv-2504-01106.description: Abstract Resetting a system’s state plays a fundamental role in physics, engineering, computer science, and many other fields. Here we focus on a method originally proposed in automata theory. The state of an automaton evolves according to a set of rules. These rules form an alphabet, and one can apply these rules one after another.

arxiv-2510-08124.title: Timeline Problems in Temporal Graphs: Vertex Cover vs. Dominating Set
arxiv-2510-08124.creator: Anton Herrmann, Christian Komusiewicz, Nils Morawietz, Frank Sommer
arxiv-2510-08124.description: Abstract A temporal graph is a finite sequence of graphs, called snapshots, over the same vertex set. Many temporal graph problems turn out to be much more difficult than their static counterparts. One such problem is Timeline Vertex Cover (also known as MinTimeline ∞ ), a temporal analogue to the classical Vertex Cover problem.

arxiv-2602-13849.title: Push-Placement: A Hybrid Approach Integrating Prehensile and Non-Prehensile Manipulation for Object Rearrangement * Equal contribution
arxiv-2602-13849.creator: Majid Sadeghinejad * , Arman Barghi * , Hamed Hosseini, Mehdi Tale Masouleh, Ahmad Kalhor
arxiv-2602-13849.description: Abstract Efficient tabletop rearrangement remains challenging due to collisions and the need for temporary buffering when target poses are obstructed. Prehensile pick-and-place provides precise control but often requires extra moves, whereas non-prehensile pushing can be more efficient but suffers from complex, imprecise dynamics.

pmc-11353045.title: The Relationship between Maternal Smoking and Infant Birth Weight: Improving Accuracy through Urine Cotinine Analysis and Effective Medical Record Strategies
pmc-11353045.creator: Danica Vojisavljevic, Donna Rudd, Roger Smith, Yogavijayan Kandasamy, Joaquim M B Pinheiro
pmc-11353045.description: Objective: We conducted a study to determine if antenatally collected maternal urine cotinine (a metabolite of nicotine) measurements can be used to assess the neonatal impact of nicotine exposure during pregnancy. This was a prospective longitudinal cohort of mother–infant dyads. Only term singleton pregnancies were included.

pmc-12583081.title: Biomechanical and clinical evaluation of 3D-printed integrated tibial prosthesis for reconstructing AORI type Ⅲ tibial plateau defects
pmc-12583081.creator: Yong Wang, Xiaoyu Zhou, Lin Guo
pmc-12583081.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo compare the biomechanical stability and clinical efficacy of 3D-printed integrated tibial prosthesis (ITP) and traditional modular augment prostheses (MAP) in reconstructing AORI Type Ⅲ tibial plateau defects, and to provide a reference for clinical decision-making.MethodsA finite element model of AORI Type Ⅲ tibial plateau defect (defect area >60%, depth >20 mm) was established using CT data of a healthy male subject. Four groups of models were constructed: Spacer, Cone, Sleeve, and ITP.

pmc-12627406.title: Rapid and minimally invasive preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidies (PGT-A) based on polar body and nanopore sequencing: a viable alternative to conventional trophectoderm-based PGT-A?
pmc-12627406.creator: Di Song, Taoli Ding, Tuan Li, Peng Zhang, Yangyun Zou, Yuanbo Hu, Hong Ye, Yajun Xu, Shengnan Wang, Tuanping Zhou, Sijia Lu, Hongli Yan
pmc-12627406.description: STUDY QUESTIONCan third-generation sequencing (TGS)-based polar body (PB) analysis serve as a viable alternative to conventional trophectoderm (TE) biopsy for preimplantation genetic testing for aneuploidy (PGT-A)?SUMMARY ANSWERThis study demonstrates the feasibility of using TGS and PB biopsy for clinical PGT-A, particularly in advanced maternal age (AMA) patients.

pmc-12719400.title: Association Between U‐p53AZ Blood Biomarker and White Matter Microstructure in Early Alzheimer's Disease: A Cross‐Sectional Study Using AlzoSure® Predict
pmc-12719400.creator: Hamide Nasiri, Setayesh Farahani, Mehrdad Mozafar, Yasaman Ghiasi, Atousa Moghadam Fard, Nasim Naseri, Amirhossein Khodadadi, Ali Salimi Asl, Maryam Mirzapour, Hossein Hamidi, Fatemeh Jafarirazi, Navid Dinarvand
pmc-12719400.description: Background and AimsAlzheimer's disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by early microstructural white matter (WM) damage, often preceding clinical symptoms. While cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) biomarkers provide valuable insights into AD pathology, they are invasive and may not reflect early WM changes.

pmc-13145554.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A2170 TRANSTHYRETIN AS A BIOMARKER FOR POST-STROKE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT: INSIGHTS FROM DIMERIZATION AND THYROID HORMONE SIGNALING
pmc-13145554.creator: Zhiyu Leng, Xiaoyi Jiang, Ming Yuan, Qinxue Sun, Yuhualei Pan, Gang Li
pmc-13145554.description: Background and aimsEffective prediction and treatment of post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remain challenging. Transthyretin (TTR), known clinically as prealbumin, functions as a neuroprotective thyroid hormone carrier. However, its role and structural dynamics in PSCI are still unclear.MethodsA PSCI mouse model was established via distal of Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion with hypoxia. Cognitive function and hippocampal long-term potentiation (LTP) were evaluated.

pmc-13157579.title: Comprehensive genomic landscape of ERBB2 in Chinese GI tumors: mutation-centered landscapes and precision treatment opportunities
pmc-13157579.creator: Yinan Shi, Xiaoxuan Wang, Xiaotong Xi, Mengxiao Wang, Jinfang Guo, Xing Zhang, Dongsheng Chen, Wenhui Yang
pmc-13157579.description: Background:ERBB2 aberrations are established oncogenic drivers with validated therapeutic relevance in breast cancer and emerging indications across solid tumors. In gastrointestinal malignancies, the prevalence, molecular contexts, and therapeutic implications of ERBB2 alterations remain incompletely defined, particularly for mutation-driven (non-amplified) disease.

pmc-13230883.title: Evaluation of quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.) genotypes using genotype by trait (GT) and genotype by yield × trait (GYT) methods
pmc-13230883.creator: Amir Forghani Saravani, Babak Rabiei, Ebrahim Souri Laki
pmc-13230883.description: Quinoa (Chenopodium quinoa Willd.), a native South American crop with high nutritional value, is a promising option for sustainable agriculture in arid and semi-arid regions of Iran, due to its environmental tolerance and valuable composition. This study aimed to evaluate quinoa genotypes using genotype by trait (GT) and genotype by yield × trait (GYT) graphical methods.

pmc-13540067.title: Congenital encephalomeningocele presenting as a giant orbital mass in a neonate: a case report
pmc-13540067.creator: Xiangxiang Chen, Yanyan Ni, Canyang Zhan
pmc-13540067.description: BackgroundCongenital orbital masses encompass a broad spectrum of etiologies, among which encephalomeningocele is exceedingly rare and particularly diagnostically challenging when atypical.Case presentationWe report a 2-hour-old female neonate who presented with a giant left orbital mass causing marked proptosis. Imaging revealed a mixed cystic-solid lesion with calcifications and septations, but no bony defect was identified preoperatively.
